security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many false positives from Markdown code fences and non-executable examples. Confirmed risks are user-facing upgrade examples that run package managers, npx tools, remote fetches, git operations, and bulk source rewrites. No prompt injection, credential handling, or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Command examples can modify dependencies, lock files, branches, and local project state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to request user confirmation before running install, audit fix, npx, git, curl, or force-install commands.

remediation.issue: The migration script example writes files across a source glob.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend dry runs, backups, scoped file selection, and human review before applying automated source rewrites.

content.value_statement: Major dependency updates can break builds, tests, and runtime behavior. This skill guides staged upgrades, compatibility checks, and validation plans for safer releases.
actual_capabilities: Explains semantic versioning ranges and major upgrade impact.
Guides dependency audits with npm, yarn, and npm-check-updates.
Plans incremental upgrades with tests after each dependency change.
Provides examples for compatibility matrices and migration scripts.
Covers Renovate, Dependabot, lock files, peer dependencies, and rollback planning.
Lists unit, integration, visual, and end-to-end testing checks.
limitations: Does not verify package-specific breaking changes without current changelogs.
Requires project tests and local commands to confirm upgrade results.
Examples focus mainly on JavaScript, React, npm, and yarn ecosystems.
Cannot guarantee production safety without staging validation and monitoring.

use_cases.title: Plan a Framework Upgrade
use_cases.description: Create an ordered plan for moving a frontend application across major framework versions.

use_cases.title: Control Automated Updates
use_cases.description: Set rules for Renovate or Dependabot so routine updates stay separate from major migrations.

use_cases.title: Fix Vulnerable Packages
use_cases.description: Upgrade security-sensitive dependencies while preserving rollback options and release validation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Current Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dependency-upgrade skill to review my current dependencies. Identify outdated packages, risky updates, and a staged checklist. Ask before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Major Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dependency-upgrade skill to plan a major framework upgrade. Include compatibility checks, peer dependency risks, test steps, and rollback criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Peer Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dependency-upgrade skill to analyze peer dependency conflicts after an upgrade. Explain the safest resolution order and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Upgrade Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dependency-upgrade skill to design Renovate or Dependabot rules for this repository. Separate patch, minor, and major updates with review gates.

output_examples.input: I need to upgrade React 17 to React 18 in a TypeScript app.
output_examples.output: The response outlines version checks, peer dependency review, React 18 migration notes, test updates, staged commits, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Dependabot opened five major update pull requests at once.
output_examples.output: The response groups updates by risk, recommends a safe merge order, separates test requirements, and identifies which updates need manual review.

output_examples.input: My package manager reports peer dependency conflicts after an upgrade.
output_examples.output: The response identifies likely version mismatches, suggests compatible version ranges, and defines verification steps before merging changes.

best_practices: Upgrade one major dependency at a time and run tests after each change.
Read changelogs, migration guides, and peer dependency notes before applying updates.
Use branches, lock files, staging validation, and rollback plans for every major upgrade.
anti_patterns: Do not upgrade all dependencies in one unreviewed change.
Do not ignore peer dependency warnings or force installs without analysis.
Do not deploy major dependency changes without regression testing and monitoring.

faq.question: What ecosystems does this skill cover best?
faq.answer: It is strongest for JavaScript projects that use npm, yarn, React, Renovate, or Dependabot.

faq.question: Can it run dependency upgrades automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command examples and plans, but users should approve local commands before changes are made.

faq.question: Does it replace package migration guides?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize the work, but current package changelogs and migration guides remain required.

faq.question: How does it reduce upgrade risk?
faq.answer: It recommends incremental updates, compatibility checks, repeated tests, rollback planning, and staging validation.

faq.question: Can it help with security updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan vulnerable package upgrades while separating urgent fixes from broader major migrations.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the package manager, current dependency files, target versions, test commands, release constraints, and known compatibility issues.
